candidates.title: News photos: CSX Santa Train gets patriotic
candidates.excerpt: KINGSPORT, Tenn. — The CSX Santa Train, an Appalachian tradition dating to its Clinchfield Railroad debut in 1943, featured the railroad’s two America 250 locomotives on Saturday, Nov. 21, during its annual 110-mile trip through Kentucky, Virginia, and Tennessee on. CM44AH locomotives Nos. 250 and 2025, along with one of the railroad’s executive train F40s, led the journey from Shelby, Ky., to Kingsport. The Kingsport Times News reports that during its 84th trip, the train distributed more than 15,000 toys, 6,000 train safety books, and 5,700 backpacks filled with gifts, gloves, and hats. “With that many years going on, we have families coming back over and over, and then they bring their kids, and then they bring their grandkids,” Angela Costa, CSX senior manager of community investment, told the newspaper. “CSX is just so excited to continue that tradition with the 2026 CSX Santa Train.” — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com. candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd introduces Vietnam equipment surcharge
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd will introduce an Equipment Imbalance Surcharge (EIS) on intra-Asia shipments to Vietnam. The surcharge will apply to dry and refrigerated containers loaded on sailings commencing from 1 December 2026. It will remain in effect until further notice. The EIS will apply in addition to relevant ocean freight, bunker-related and security surcharges, Terminal Handling Charges and any applicable local or contingency charges.

candidates.title: Maersk raises UK and Ireland intermodal fuel fees
candidates.excerpt: Maersk has announced revised Intermodal Fuel Fee levels for full-container-load landside transportation in the United Kingdom and Ireland during December 2026. In the United Kingdom, the fee will be 11.6% for transport by truck or rail. Ireland’s fee will be 8.1% for truck transportation. The revised fees apply to non-FMC shipments from 1 December 2026. For FMC-regulated shipments, they will take effect on 20 December. For non-FMC shipments, Maersk will determine the applicable Price Calculation Date using the estimated departure of the first vessel shown in the latest booking confirmation issued at the customer’s request. For containers booked under a port or Container Yard Bill of Lading, the calculation date will be based on the delivery or collection date. Maersk noted that customers with bespoke pricing may face higher rates, which will be communicated by their account managers.

candidates.title: Cool Carriers takes delivery of world-first gate-rudder reefer
candidates.excerpt: Cool Carriers has taken delivery of Snow Land, the third vessel in its seven-ship Snow-class newbuilding programme. Kitanihon Shipbuilding delivered the ice-class vessel in Japan on 12 November 2026. According to Cool Carriers, Snow Land is the world’s first specialised refrigerated cargo vessel equipped with a gate rudder. The Gate Rudder System replaces the conventional single rudder behind the propeller with two high-lift foil rudders positioned on either side of it. During voyages, water flowing across the rudder blades generates additional forward thrust, allowing the vessel to maintain speed while consuming less fuel. Each blade can also be controlled separately to improve manoeuvrability during berthing operations. Wärtsilä, a licensee of the technology, has reported fuel savings of up to 20% on vessels using the system. Kitanihon Shipbuilding said Snow Land’s overall design achieves a carbon dioxide intensity approximately 50% below the reference level for a vessel of its type

candidates.title: Swire Shipping reduces feeder surcharge for Indian Subcontinent trades
candidates.excerpt: Swire Shipping will reduce its Feeder and Equipment Surcharge (FES) for selected trades involving the Indian Subcontinent. The revised surcharge will apply to Bills of Lading with an on-board date on or after 20 November 2026. Trades regulated by the US Federal Maritime Commission remain subject to the applicable regulatory notice period. Swire Shipping introduced the FES on 1 April 2026 to cover the use of feeder partners that extend its network beyond its core service areas. Under the revised structure, exports from the Indian Subcontinent will be subject to charges of US$175 for all 20-foot containers and US$350 for 20-foot reefers. Rates for all 40-foot containers and 40-foot reefers will be US$350 and US$700, respectively. For imports into the Indian Subcontinent, the surcharge will be US$150 for all 20-foot containers, US$500 for 20-foot reefers, US$300 for all 40-foot containers and US$1,000 for 40-foot reefers. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%. candidates.title: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom
candidates.excerpt: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom Private credit is gaining ground in Asia as demand for flexible capital grows and the AI boom needs funding, according to KKR. Asia has historically relied on banks for credit, and they still provide 88 per cent of the region’s debt capital, compared with 50 per cent in Europe and just 31 per cent in the US. However, forces reshaping Japan and driving investment in AI infrastructure are starting to change this, KKR said in a recent blog post. In the US and Europe, regulators have made banks retrench, but that is not happening in Asia. Instead, private credit is in demand across the region because it offers flexible capital alongside banks that remain deeply embedded in corporate financing. KKR argued that Asian banks provide cheap but inflexible capital, and that private credit was plugging this gap. The Amsterdam-based fintech business, which serves 300,000 businesses, has introduced a business overdraft and credit card, offering personalised limits of up to €20,000 (£16,700) and €40,000, respectively. The products use customers’ existing transaction data to make credit decisions in seconds, removing the need for businesses to submit annual accounts or bank statements. Finom said more than half of its customers now qualify for credit under the new offering, compared with between 11 per cent and 17 per cent under its previous credit product.
